headline: Alpine Access via the Meadows in the Sky Parkway
reservation: A valid National Park entry pass is required for all visitors. While there is currently no reservation system for the Parkway, access to the summit area is seasonally restricted by snowmelt and road conditions; check the official Parks Canada site for the seasonal opening status of the upper gates.

days.title: Rainforest to Alpine Ascent

stops.name: Giant Cedars Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk through an ancient grove of Western Red Cedars, some over half a millennium old, located just off the highway.

stops.name: Skunk Cabbage Boardwalk
stops.detail: Explore the wetlands along the Illecillewaet River, ideal for spotting migratory birds in early summer.

days.driving: Allow 30–40 minutes for highway stops; conditions vary with mountain weather.
days.note: The lower boardwalks are generally accessible earlier in the season than the summit road.

days.title: Meadows in the Sky
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Parkway Entrance

stops.name: Balsam Lake
stops.detail: Park at the upper limit and take the seasonal shuttle or walk to the summit area to see subalpine wildflower displays.

stops.name: Fire Lookout
stops.detail: Visit the historic 1927 station for 360-degree views of the Selkirk and Monashee mountain ranges.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour to drive the winding 26km Parkway; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: Vehicle length restrictions apply on the switchbacks; check official limits for trailers or large RVs.

days.title: Monashee Vistas

stops.name: Eva Lake Trail
stops.detail: Trek through the rolling subalpine terrain to reach a pristine glacial lake surrounded by talus slopes.

stops.name: Nels Nelsen Historic Ski Jump
stops.detail: View the site of world-record ski jumps near the base of the mountain and learn about the area's sporting history.

days.driving: Minimal driving within the park; allow 20 minutes for local transfers.
days.note: Eva Lake is a full-day commitment; ensure you have sufficient daylight for the return journey.

intel.title: Seasonal Parkway Gates
intel.text: The Meadows in the Sky Parkway is paved but only fully opens to the summit when snow is cleared, typically from July to September. Lower sections may open earlier in the spring.

intel.title: Wildflower Peak
intel.text: The famous subalpine bloom at the summit typically peaks in early to mid-August. Plan for mid-week visits to avoid the busiest periods on the narrow upper trails.

intel.title: Summit Turnaround
intel.text: The Balsam Lake parking area at the top of the Parkway is small and serves as the hub for the summit shuttle. Large vehicles should use designated pullouts lower on the mountain.

intel.title: Canyon Shadow
intel.text: Signal is lost quickly once you begin the ascent on the Parkway. The town of Revelstoke is the last reliable point for digital communication.

intel.title: Mountain Grades
intel.text: Ensure your tank is full in Revelstoke before starting the 26km climb, as the steep grade increases fuel consumption significantly. There are no services on the Parkway.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental in Kelowna and drive 2.5 hours east; Revelstoke serves as the primary supply hub for groceries and outdoor permits.
plan.vehicle: The Parkway is paved but features sharp switchbacks; trailers and long motorhomes are prohibited beyond certain points.
plan.goldenHour: The Monashee Lookout on the Parkway offers expansive westward views for sunset, depending on seasonal cloud cover.
